comment: Files under apps/mobile/app/ that are shell CHROME, not navigable content screens — exempt from the ROUTES-manifest closure in tools/check-route-manifest.mjs. Every allow entry must be {"name": <app/-relative file, extension omitted>, "reason": non-empty string}; an entry without a reviewed reason is a gate bypass. Content screens NEVER belong here — register them in apps/mobile/src/routes.ts so the states sweep, the Maestro device flows and the startup budgets cover them. Layout files (_layout.*), +html.* and API routes are router plumbing the gate excludes by pattern and never need listing. unreachableStates is the second reviewed escape: a ROUTES entry may declare a states value of null ONLY when a {"route", "state", "reason"} row here documents why that state provably cannot occur (e.g. a screen whose data source is a static in-process registry has no loading or error state) — the honest alternative to a fabricated spinner. Stale rows (the route gone, or the state declared with a real test id again) fail the gate.

allow.name: sign-in
allow.reason: auth chrome, not content: the mode-aware sign-in surface (stub or PKCE) has no canonical data states — its pending/failure handling is covered by the sign-in RNTL suite, and it must stay reachable to the SIGNED-OUT user the route manifest's data-state contract presumes away

allow.name: perf-harness
allow.reason: dev-only measurement chrome, not content: the CI device lane deep-links here with budget params from tools/interaction-budget.json and asserts the self-measured perf-pass/perf-fail leaf marker (tools/check-e2e-device.mjs). No canonical data states — the probes run against the in-process actions registry, never a query — and outside __DEV__ the screen renders only its unavailability note

allow.name: +not-found
allow.reason: expo-router's unmatched-route convention file — REQUIRED chrome (the gate reds on its ABSENCE) rather than a registrable screen: no data states, only a way home. Pattern-excluded from route enumeration; listed here because src/routes.ts documents it as chrome and this file is where chrome is reviewed
